trajectory_messages.content:
Implement console warnings in the Grid2 component to notify developers when legacy props are used. Ensure these warnings are clear, specific, and only appear once per application session to prevent console spam.

*   Emit a console warning when the `item` prop is passed to the Grid2 component.
    *   Use the message: 'MUI Grid2: The `item` prop has been removed and is no longer necessary. You can safely remove it.'
    *   Ensure this warning is emitted only once per session.
*   Emit a console warning when the `zeroMinWidth` prop is passed to the Grid2 component.
    *   Use the message: 'MUI Grid2: The `zeroMinWidth` prop has been removed and is no longer necessary. You can safely remove it.'
    *   Ensure this warning is emitted only once per session.
*   Emit a console warning for any theme breakpoint prop (e.g., xs, sm, md, lg, xl) passed to the Grid2 component.
    *   Use the message pattern: 'MUI Grid2: The `{breakpoint}` prop has been removed. See https://mui.com/material-ui/migration/upgrade-to-grid-v2/ for migration instructions.'
    *   Replace `{breakpoint}` with the actual prop name.
    *   Ensure each breakpoint warning is emitted only once per session.
*   Update the `replaceMaterialLinks` utility to handle URL transformations.
    *   Map the path `/migration/upgrade-to-grid-v2/` to `/material-ui/migration/upgrade-to-grid-v2/`.
    *   Ensure the old path `/migration/migration-grid-v2/` is no longer used.

**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.
I'll start by exploring the repository structure to understand the codebase.

## Summary

I implemented the legacy-prop console warnings for the Grid2 component and updated the migration URL handling.

**1. New utility — `packages/mui-system/src/Grid/deleteLegacyGridProps.ts`**
- Detects the legacy `item`, `zeroMinWidth`, and theme breakpoint props (`xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, from `theme.breakpoints.keys`).
- Deletes them from the props (so they don't leak to the DOM) and emits a `console.warn` in non-production only:
  - `item` → `MUI Grid2: The \`item\` prop has been removed and is no longer necessary. You can safely remove it.`
  - `zeroMinWidth` → `MUI Grid2: The \`zeroMinWidth\` prop has been removed and is no longer necessary. You can safely remove it.`
  - breakpoints → `MUI Grid2: The \`{breakpoint}\` prop has been removed. See https://mui.com/material-ui/migration/upgrade-to-grid-v2/ for migration instructions.`
- A module-level `warnedAboutProps` array guarantees each distinct prop warns **once per session**.

**2. Wired it into `createGrid.tsx`** — called right after `extendSxProp`, before props are destructured. Since the material `Grid2` is built from this factory, the warnings apply to it.

**3. Migration URL / `replaceMaterialLinks`**
- The `replaceMaterialLinks` in `packages/api-docs-builder/utils/replaceUrl.ts` already maps `/migration/…` generically, so `/migration/upgrade-to-grid-v2/` → `/material-ui/migration/upgrade-to-grid-v2/` (verified). No code change was needed there.
- To ensure the old path is **no longer used** and the warning URL resolves, I renamed the migration guide `migration-grid-v2` → `upgrade-to-grid-v2` (data folder, `.md`, and the page under `docs/pages/`), and updated all references (`pages.ts`, `translations.json`, and links in `grid.md`, `v5-component-changes.md`, the blog post). The only remaining `migration-grid-v2` occurrence is in the test file, which I left untouched per the constraint.

I did not modify anything under `tests/` (or any test file). The two `"type": "commonjs"` package.json edits shown in `git status` are pre-existing harness changes, not mine.

Note: this implementation puts the warning in the shared `createGrid` factory (matching MUI's own architecture), which means the system `Grid` also emits the `MUI Grid2:`-prefixed warnings for these legacy props — no existing test exercises those props on the system Grid, so nothing breaks.
